highlights.title: A0538-66: A transient ultraluminous X-ray source with a relativistic outflow, 69ms pulsations, and anomalous optical activity
highlights.reason: 该工作报道了大麦哲伦云著名 Be/X 射线双星 A0538-66 在沉寂约 45 年后重返超爱丁顿光度（$L_{\rm X} \approx 1.5\times 10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$）的超亮 X 射线脉冲星（ULXP）爆发。高分辨率光谱探测到速度高达 $v_{\rm LOS} \approx -0.12c$ 的相对论超爱丁顿外流，并确证了 $69\,\mathrm{ms}$ 的脉动演化以及反常的光学-X射线去耦现象，为揭示中子星超临界吸积动力学与漏斗几何遮蔽效应提供了关键观测锚点。

highlights.title: Tidal Excitation of Relativistic Stars
highlights.reason: 该工作首次构建了相对论致密星在含时潮汐外力驱动下的完全因果格林函数与准正则模（QNM）正交展开理论，解决了相对论非厄米辐射系统无法使用简正模展开的基础难题，对中子星双星潮汐共振激发、引力波波形建模及动态 Love 数物理机制有重大理论价值。

highlights.title: Evidence for Distinct One-Off and Repeating Subpopulations in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2
highlights.reason: 该工作利用模拟推断（SBI）框架对 CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 进行星族统计建模，首次在统计上决定性地证实了 FRB 存在独立的本质单发（truly one-off）和重复（repeating）两个子星族，并给出了重复源总数上限及体积发生率，直接关乎 FRB 起源与中心引擎的本质划分。

highlights.title: From Giant Envelopes to Rapidly Contracting Cores in Rotating Population III Stars from $500$ to $1000 \, M_\odot$
highlights.reason: 本文利用 GENEC 详细模拟了 $500\text{--}1000\,M_\odot$ 自转 Pop III 超大质量恒星演化至硅耗尽阶段的终极结构与角动量状态，定量排除了其坍缩时形成离心自支撑吸积盘产生长 GRB/喷流的传统假设，并评估了对不稳定超新星判定及富氮星风反馈，对研究超新星前身星引擎、黑洞种子及极早期化学增丰具有重要参考价值。

highlights.title: Universal relations for hybrid stars and their quark cores: a systematic scan of the quark-matter parameter space
highlights.reason: 该工作系统扫描了包含强子-夸克一阶相变的致密星参数空间，证明了混合星表面观测量（如 $I$-Love 关系）高度伪装成纯强子中子星（偏差 $<0.5\%$），同时导出了夸克核边界处具有普适标度律的解析展开关系（如 $\Lambda_C \propto \mathcal{C}_C^{-4}$）与全星归一化质量剖面公式。这对致密天体状态方程限制、引力波潮汐形变推断以及中子星内部夸克核反演具有直接理论参考价值。

highlights.title: Radio and Gamma-Ray Timing of a Newly Discovered Millisecond Pulsar
highlights.reason: 该工作报道了对新发现毫秒脉冲星 PSR J2147$-$3604 的射电与伽马射线多波段联合测时，证认了未关联 Fermi 伽马射线源 4FGL J2146.9$-$3606，并测定了其轨道动力学参量、法拉第旋转量与星际介质闪烁特性，为致密天体多波段观测与测时阵列源库提供了高精度样本。

highlights.title: Scaling Up: A Global Optical/X-ray Correlation For Reprocessing Across Black Hole Masses
highlights.reason: 该工作建立了跨越恒星级双星（XRBs）到超大质量黑洞（AGN）近10个量级的全局光学/X射线热再辐射定标律，论证了由X射线照射薄盘驱动的光学光变标度不变性，为黑洞吸积盘-冕几何与多波段辐射耦合提供了统一经验框架，与黑洞吸积及高能辐射机制密切相关。

highlights.title: Discovery of 51 pulsars in a reanalysis of the Green Bank North Celestial Cap Survey and a revised pulsar census
highlights.reason: 该工作利用 GPU 加速的 FFT 谐波搜索与针对慢脉冲星的直接折叠搜索方法（DFSM），对 GBNCC 巡天 350 MHz 归档数据进行全面重处理，成功确认了 51 颗新射电脉冲星（含 1 颗双星 MSP），并揭示了部分源的色散量超出 NE2025/YMW16 模型极大值的现象，为低频致密天体普查、射电掩食及银河系自由电子分布与 DM 测量提供了实用样本与搜索方法学参考。

highlights.title: Internal Nucleon Properties and the Equation of State of Ultra-Dense Matter
highlights.reason: 文章探讨将单个核子的手征孤子模型内部性质映射到中子星等超密冷物质状态方程（EoS）的可行性，系统检验了正则与 Belinfante 能动张量（EMT）下的机械压强 $p^{\rm mec}$ 与热力学压强 $p^{\rm th}$ 的对应关系，指出直接局部映射因忽略表面能和剪切力项而存在内在矛盾与因果律破缺（$c_s^2 > 1$），对理解致密天体微观物理输入与夸克去禁闭状态方程的唯象构建具有参考价值。

highlights.title: Observational evidence of black hole event horizon from ultra-compact X-ray binaries
highlights.reason: 文章利用白矮星伴星超紧凑X射线双星（UCXBs）中由纯引力辐射主导轨道演化并精确决定质量转移率 $\dot{M}$ 的特性，直接对比同吸积率下黑洞（47 Tuc X-9）与中子星系统的辐射效率 $\eta = \overline{L}_{\rm X}/(\dot{M} c^2)$，为致密天体高能吸积物理与事件视界存在性提供了稳健的观测证据。

highlights.title: The Promise of Gravitational-Wave Astronomy
highlights.reason: 该综述系统梳理了从高频地基干涉仪到空间低频和纳赫兹引力波波段的天体物理学前景，直接关联研究组关注的致密双星并合多信使物理（sGRB/千新星）、核心坍缩超新星（CCSN）中心引擎动力学、原初中子星振荡与中微子辐射机制。

highlights.title: Finite-Temperature Equations of State for Neutron-Star Mergers within the Quark Mean-Field Model
highlights.reason: 文章构建了双中子星合并关键微观物理所需的夸克平均场（QMF）有限温状态方程，给出了热指数 $\Gamma_{\rm th}$ 的高精度解析参数化，直接关联双中子星并合后残余天体演化、引力波特征峰频 $f_{\rm peak}$ 及坍缩阈值。

highlights.title: Low-frequency spectra and scattering of pulsars towards the Gum Nebula with the MWA
highlights.reason: 该工作利用 MWA-VCS 在 80–240 MHz 对古姆星云（Gum Nebula）方向 6 颗脉冲星开展低频能谱截断与脉冲散射展宽的联合观测与建模，定量揭示了电离介质中自由-自由吸收测度与散射测度之间的物理脱耦关系，对评估银河系大尺度电离结构、校准自由电子密度模型（YMW16 与 NE2025）及理解 FRB 视线传播效应具有直接参考价值。

highlights.title: Fast Radio Bursts from Monster Shocks and Flares of Inspiraling Binary Neutron Stars: A Kinetic Model for Double Pulsar
highlights.reason: 该研究利用三维全动理学相对论 PIC 模拟探讨双中子星并合前轨道运动驱动磁层相互作用产生 FRB 的相干辐射机制，直接关乎本组对 FRB 前兆暴及致密天体高能瞬变源机制的研究兴趣。

highlights.title: Cell-based theoretical criteria on the onset and stability limit of thermonuclear detonation
highlights.reason: 本文将地面燃烧学中的爆轰胞格尺寸 $\lambda$ 理论判据引入白矮星热核爆炸（Ia 型超新星），给出了氦碳包层与碳氧核心爆轰稳定传播的临界压力标高 $H_{\rm p,crit} = 0.556\lambda$ 及起爆能量 $E_{\rm min}$ 的解析标度律，为超新星中心引擎点火与数值模拟网格效应提供了坚实的物理判据。

highlights.title: Two sides of the same spin: tracking optical and radio pulsations of SAX J1808.4-3658 from outburst to quiescence
highlights.reason: 该工作结合 TNG/SiFAP2 超快速光学测时、NICER X 射线、LCO 测光监测与 MeerKAT 射电相干搜寻，对吸积毫秒脉冲星 SAX J1808.4-3658 从 2022 年爆发到宁静态进行了多波段协同追踪，揭示了光学脉动相对于 X 射线的动态时延与反相关标度关系，为吸积盘-磁层相互作用区中的相对论粒子加速与非热辐射机制提供了坚实的观测约束。

highlights.title: Broadband non-thermal emission predictions based on 3D simulations of supernova explosions within active galactic nuclei jets
highlights.reason: 本文基于3D相对论流体模拟后处理计算了AGN喷流与超新星抛射物相互作用的宽波段非热辐射（同步辐射与逆康普顿），提供了激波加速能谱特征与空间形态，对探讨致密环境SN、相对论喷流激波辐射及射电星系结（如M87 Knot A）物理有直接参考价值。

highlights.title: The ePESSTO+ census of ZTF nuclear transients. I. What flares in galactic nuclei?
highlights.reason: 该研究基于 ZTF 警报流对星系核区瞬变源开展了无测光先验的实时筛选与普查，系统量化了超新星（SNe Ia/II/Ib/c）作为核心背景污染与潮汐瓦解事件（TDE）在颜色演化率和上升时标上的可测分界，为核区致密天体爆发及超新星的早期判异提供了实测依据。

highlights.title: Multimessenger Constraints on Nuclear Acceleration in Neutrino-Emitting Seyfert Coronae
highlights.reason: 文章系统探讨了高能中微子发射源 NGC 1068 与 NGC 7469 冕区中的重核加速与多信使级联过程，给出了核成分份额 $f_{\rm nuc}$ 与冕区参数的明确联合观测限制，对致密天体冕区粒子加速与中微子辐射物理具有参考价值。

highlights.title: The compact jets of the black hole X-ray binary Swift J1753.5-0127 during its 2023-2024 outburst
highlights.reason: 该工作通过 MeerKAT、AMI-LA、Swift、NICER 等对短周期黑洞低质量 X 射线双星 Swift J1753.5–0127 的暗弱、纯硬态双峰爆发开展了密集的多波段监测，系统解析了致密相对论喷流的射电演化、吸积盘强截断特性以及射电-X射线光度相关性（$L_{\mathrm{R}}$–$L_{\mathrm{X}}$）在混合/离群黑洞双星中的几何约束机制，对研究致密天体吸积-喷流耦合具有重要参考价值。

highlights.title: Seeing Double: The Theory Defying Twin Flares of TDE 2022dbl
highlights.reason: 该工作针对重复部分潮汐瓦解事件（pTDE）候选体 TDE 2022dbl 两次爆发（间隔约 700 天）及第三次爆发缺失的矛盾，结合多波段测光、X 射线限制与高分辨率光谱，揭示了碎屑流与先前留存吸积盘相互作用（stream-disk interaction）以及弹道式核心重构（ballistic core reformation）引起轨道周期的改变，对理解致密天体潮汐撕裂、吸积盘演化和轨道动力学反冲具有重要参考价值。

entries.title: MRI Turbulence versus $α$-Viscosity in Circumbinary Disks: Implications for Gravitational-Wave Dephasing and Accretion Variability
entries.abstract: Our understanding of gas torques on massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) relies on hydrodynamical (HD) simulations of circumbinary disks (CBDs) in which an $α$-viscosity models angular momentum transport. However, CBDs around MBHBs near merger are hot, magnetized plasmas where transport is driven by magnetohydrodynamical (MHD) turbulence sustained by the magnetorotational instability (MRI). We test how well an $α$-viscosity captures MRI turbulence with 3D global Athena++ simulations of a locally isothermal CBD around an equal-mass, circular MBHB, run in HD and MHD from the same initial torus on identical grids, so that only the transport mechanism differs. Excising the region within twice the binary separation, $r<2~a_{\rm bin}$, allows $1000$ orbits of evolution, several times longer than previous MHD simulations. Both disks deliver the same accretion rate, and the gas beyond $2~a_{\rm bin}$ exerts a positive torque in both, yet the MHD torque is $3.5$ times larger and $3$ times more variable. Near the midplane, transport is similar in the disk body but three times weaker in MHD at the cavity edge, where $2$-$3$ times more mass piles up in a more eccentric cavity, raising the torque. The accretion rate is modulated mainly at twice the binary frequency in HD, but by a persistent lump at the cavity edge and its beat with the binary in MHD. The outer-disk torque therefore implies a contribution to the gas-induced phase shift in the gravitational-wave signal of LISA binaries $3.5$ times larger than in $α$-disk models, and a different variability signature for LSST and Roman.

entries.title: Magnetic field evolution in feedback-dominated galaxies
entries.abstract: Over the last decade, magnetic fields (B-fields) have become a common ingredient in galaxy formation simulations. Although seemingly unimportant in matching observational constraints such as the $M_*-M_{\rm halo}$ relations, the B-field influences the circumgalactic medium (CGM) gas and determines cosmic ray (CR) propagation, making it an indispensable non-thermal component. Nevertheless, the intricate physics of B-fields, particularly how they evolve to the observed $μ$G-level field, remains largely elusive. In this work, we systematically address the evolution of B-fields over cosmic time using the FIRE-2 (Feedback In Realistic Environments) magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) simulations. We present results for both Milky Way (MW)-mass and dwarf galaxies, with and without CRs. We find that CRs have little impact on B-field properties, while the halo mass controls the saturated B-field strength at $z\sim 0$. However, all runs reach a halo-independent magnetic-to-turbulent ratio of $f_{\rm B}\sim 1-10\%$, though the methods used to measure turbulence could affect this value. We identify a three-stage evolutionary course for the B-field in tandem with galaxy formation: i. expansion, ii. amplification, and iii. saturation. The feature is universal, though the timings depend on the initial location and star formation history of the gas. Flux-freezing is the predominant driver for the first and last stages, exhibiting power relations $B\sim ρ^{2/3}$ and $ρ^{1/2}$, although the latter could also be explained by dynamical and energetic equilibria. The intermediate amplification stage, potentially driven by ``dynamos'', is fuelled by structure formation, feedback, and gas turbulence. We conjecture a numerically triggered, turbulence-driven amplification process to explain this phenomenon.

entries.title: MeV dark matter decay forecasts for the COSI mission
entries.abstract: The decay of dark matter (DM) is a generic prediction of many particle physics models, producing distinctive monochromatic signatures in environments such as the Galactic halo. Searches for decaying DM in the elusive 'MeV gap' have remained conspicuously under-explored, despite well-motivated models including axion-like particles, sterile neutrinos, and hidden-sector scenarios predicting signatures in this energy range. The upcoming Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI) telescope will help bridge this gap. Designed to probe this energy band with high spectral resolution, low background, and wide field of view, COSI is well-suited for DM line searches at the MeV scale. In this work, we make projections for COSI's 2-year sensitivity for DM decay in the Milky Way halo using dedicated all-sky simulations incorporating COSI's predicted instrument response. We conclude that COSI will improve the sensitivity to the DM lifetime by more than an order of magnitude over the DM mass range 0.4 to 10 MeV.

entries.title: From Giant Envelopes to Rapidly Contracting Cores in Rotating Population III Stars from $500$ to $1000 \, M_\odot$
entries.abstract: Population III (Pop III) stars link the chemical enrichment of the early Universe to the formation of the first massive black holes, yet their evolution remains poorly understood at extreme masses. Using GENEC, we evolve rotating zero metallicity models from $500$ to $1000\,M_\odot$ at $v/v_{\rm crit}=0.1$ through core Si burning, and a $1000\,M_\odot$, $v/v_{\rm crit}=0.4$ model evolved through He exhaustion. In the fiducial $1000\,M_\odot$ model, convection and rotational transport carry freshly synthesized C and O into H burning layers, producing $62.1\,M_\odot$ of primary N by He exhaustion. Surface mass loss removes $20.2\,M_\odot$, including $1.8\times10^{-3}\,M_\odot$ of N, with $\log(\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{O})=0.68$, $\log(\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{C})=1.48$, and $\log(\mathrm{C}/\mathrm{O})=-0.80$. By the final hydrostatic model, the inner $100\,M_\odot$ is confined within $0.088\,R_\odot$ while the photosphere remains several thousand solar radii away. As C, Ne, O, and Si burning accelerate, chemical mixing freezes out and advanced products remain buried beneath the envelope. At core Si exhaustion, the central angular velocity reaches $4\times10^{-3}\,{\rm s^{-1}}$ while the surface rotates at $5.25\times10^{-8}\,{\rm s^{-1}}$, a contrast of $7.6\times10^4$. Contraction drives this spin up, while inner specific angular momentum changes by less than $1\%$. The maximum $j_{\rm eq}/j_{\rm ISCO}$ is $0.313$, limiting disk formation in our inside out estimate. These models show that Pop~III stars can produce strong primary N signatures and rapidly rotating black hole progenitors while their envelopes determine which products enrich the early Universe.

entries.title: Universal relations for hybrid stars and their quark cores: a systematic scan of the quark-matter parameter space
entries.abstract: Universal, equation-of-state (EOS) insensitive relations among the global properties of compact stars are well established for hadronic neutron stars and for self-bound strange stars. We ask whether analogous relations hold for the quark core of a hybrid star, and whether the core can be constrained from the surface. Describing quark matter with the three-flavor MIT bag model with repulsive vector interactions, matched to the hadronic DD2 EOS through a Maxwell construction, we scan the full $(B^{1/4},G_V)$ plane and obtain 1112 hybrid EOSs with maximum masses above $2\,M_\odot$, broadly compatible with current multimessenger constraints. For every stable configuration we evaluate the mass, radius, moment of inertia, and tidal deformability both at the stellar surface and at the boundary of the quark core. Global quantities follow the relations of hadronic stars---the $I$--Love relation to within $0.5\%$---while core quantities follow those of self-bound strange stars with median deviations of $6$--$9\%$. We explain the latter by expanding the structure of the core in powers of its compactness: to first order, the core mass, baryon mass, moment of inertia, and tidal deformability depend only on the compactness and on the properties of the hadron--quark interface, chiefly the ratio $ξ=p_{\rm tr}/\varepsilon_+$ of transition pressure to quark energy density. The strange-star relations are the $ξ\to0$ member of this family, and the deviations from them measure $ξ$. The fractional core mass and radius of all configurations follow the normalized mass profile of the star, and no global observable allows the core size to be inferred. Evanescent cores dominate the viable parameter space, while sizable cores require low bag constants and strong vector couplings.

entries.title: Radio and Gamma-Ray Timing of a Newly Discovered Millisecond Pulsar
entries.abstract: We report the discovery and timing of PSR J2147-3604, a fully recycled millisecond pulsar with a spin period of 3.2 ms, discovered in a reprocessing of the 350-MHz Green Bank North Celestial Cap (GBNCC) survey and later serendipitously confirmed by the MeerKAT TRAPUM UHF survey of Fermi-LAT unidentified sources. We followed up this pulsar with Murriyang/Parkes radio telescope and obtained a phase-connected timing solution spanning one year, revealing a 4.5-day binary orbit with very low eccentricity (e ~ 1.9 x $10^{-5}$). A follow-up search in LAT data revealed gamma-ray pulsations, allowing for a joint radio and gamma-ray timing analysis. Assuming a neutron-star mass of 1.5 Msun, the inferred median companion mass (~0.2 Msun) is consistent with a helium white dwarf. The pulsar has a low dispersion measure of 17.0 pc cm$^{-3}$ and shows strong scintillation, leading to it being detected in ~72% of the observations covering the 704-1174 MHz band with Murriyang. The pulsar has a narrow duty cycle of ~6.5%, which leads to individual time of arrival (ToA) uncertainties of ~4.5 us for a 10 min integration with MeerKAT, suggesting this pulsar is well suited for inclusion in PTA experiments.

entries.title: Scaling Up: A Global Optical/X-ray Correlation For Reprocessing Across Black Hole Masses
entries.abstract: This study extends the optical/X-ray correlation from black hole low-mass X-ray binaries (XRBs) to active galactic nuclei (AGN), bridging scales from stellar-mass to supermassive black holes (SMBHs). In XRBs, optical emission predominantly originates from the thermal reprocessing of high-energy photons on the surface of the geometrically thin, optically thick accretion disk. The reprocessed optical luminosity follows a power-law relation of the form $L_{V} \propto L_{X}^β a$, with $β\sim 0.5$, where $L_X$ is the X-ray luminosity and the orbital separation $a$ serves as a proxy for the disk size. To test the universality of this relationship across all mass scales, we analyzed quasi-simultaneous X-ray and optical flux data from a sample of XRBs and AGN that have estimates of the radius of the optically emitting disk. To bridge the structural differences between these populations, we utilized the characteristic optical/X-ray time lag derived from reverberation mapping as a physical proxy for the reprocessing radius. Our analysis reveals a tight, global correlation across all black hole masses, described by $\log L_V = 0.48\log L_X + 0.96\log a_R + 6.5$ with a scatter of $\sim 0.20$ dex, where $a_R$ is the reprocessing radius derived from the lag. Incorporating a geometric correction for the disk inclination angle ($\cos i$) slightly reduces this scatter to $0.18$ dex. These results suggest that X-ray reprocessing is scale-invariant across accretion disks, from stellar-mass black holes to SMBHs. This scaling relation provides new constraints for models of X-ray emission regions in accreting black holes.

entries.title: An upper limit on Galactic OB+black hole binaries from SDSS-V
entries.abstract: Binaries composed of a luminous OB star and a black hole (BH) are a key evolutionary link between massive stellar binaries and merging compact-object binaries, but only a handful are known and their occurrence fraction remains poorly constrained. We use multi-epoch spectroscopy from the SDSS-V Milky Way Mapper to place a first rigorous empirical upper limit on the fraction of Galactic massive ($\geq 10\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) OB stars with a close BH companion, $f_\mathrm{BH}$. Radial-velocity (RV) variability alone cannot distinguish BH companions from the far more numerous luminous binaries. We therefore combine the SDSS-V RV variability measurements of 3130 massive OB stars with high-resolution follow-up and literature information to identify luminous companions among the RV-variable subset. Forward-modelling the detectability of OB+BH systems using BH masses and orbital parameters from binary-evolution models, we find $f_\mathrm{BH} \lesssim 3\%$ at 95% credibility. This empirical upper limit approaches, but does not exclude, theoretical predictions for the OB+BH fraction. The constraint is primarily limited by the number of RV-variable systems that can be decisively classified, highlighting the importance of complete, high-quality follow-up for future searches.

entries.title: Physical characteristics of the Galaxy defining the oscillation period of librating orbits near the OLR of the bar
entries.abstract:
We studied librating orbits of stars near the Outer Lindblad Resonance (OLR) of the bar using the angle-action variables of Hamiltonian dynamics. The librating orbits change the direction of their elongation relative to the major axis of the bar in a limited range of angles. To calculate orbits, we used the model of the Galaxy with an analytical bar which reproduces well the distributions of the observed stellar velocities along the Galactocentric distance R derived from the Gaia DR3 data. We compared the values of the orbital oscillation period of a typical star obtained from the theory and with the use of numerical simulation. Both values were found to be in good agreement and are equal to 2.0 Gyr. It was shown that the change in the average orbital radius, , of a star, calculated over the time interval of one radial oscillation, is regulated by the change in the direction of orbital elongation. As the orbit is tilted relative to the minor axis of the bar in the sense of Galactic rotation, the angular momentum of the star, L, decreases, on average, causing a decrease in . It turned out that the ratio of the frequency of orbit oscillations to the epicyclic frequency, omega/kappa, is determined by the parameters q_R and

entries.title: Discovery of 51 pulsars in a reanalysis of the Green Bank North Celestial Cap Survey and a revised pulsar census
entries.abstract: We present results from a reanalysis of the Green Bank North Celestial Cap (GBNCC) survey, conducted at 350 MHz with the Green Bank Telescope between 2009 and 2020, covering the sky with declinations $δ>-40^\circ$. We searched the survey data using an FFT-based periodicity search, with candidate selection extending to very low spectral signal-to-noise ratios and summing up to 32 harmonics. From the 60 promising candidates identified in this search, we confirmed 51 new pulsars using the Green bank and CHIME. We also used a direct folding search method (DFSM) to search for slow pulsars between 500 ms and 10 s. Of the 51 pulsars identified in the FFT search, 43 fall within this period range, all of which were found by the DFSM. The DFSM also found an additional pulsar that had been missed during the inspection of the FFT candidates. Most of the new discoveries are canonical pulsars, with spin periods ranging from 299 ms to 4.4 s and dispersion measures from 10 to 192 $\rm pc \, cm^{-3}$. We also found a binary millisecond pulsar with a spin period of 3.2 ms in a 4.5-d orbit. We redetected 855 pulsars in the data, 825 of which were found in the FFT search. Within the effective parameter space of our periodicity search, the FFT search recovered $\sim$98 % of the known pulsars within the survey sensitivity limits. After accounting for previously reported pulsars whose observations were not processed or whose parameters lay outside our search range, the updated GBNCC census now includes 964 pulsars.

entries.title: Graph Learning with Multiplicative Aggregation for Solar Filament Fragment Association Modeling in Full-disk H$α$ Images
entries.abstract: Solar filaments are prominent features in H$α$ observations. During their evolution, they often exhibit complex morphological and topological changes, which, due to line-of-sight projection effects, appear as fragmentation and merging. These phenomena make it difficult to reliably track solar filaments using automated methods, as the same structure may appear different over time. To address this issue, we formulate filament fragment association as a graph-based learning problem, where individual fragments are represented as nodes and candidate pairwise relationships are modeled as edges to infer whether fragments belong to the same filament. Furthermore, we propose a novel graph neural network (GNN) that incorporates multiplicative aggregation layers to enhance feature aggregation in the graph, replacing conventional additive aggregation with a multiplicative mechanism to better capture information between fragments. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves reliable performance in filament fragment association, validating the effectiveness of the graph-based formulation and the proposed multiplicative aggregation mechanism.

entries.title: Intermittency in the Multiphase ISM --- I. Extreme Density, Velocity, and Magnetic Fluctuations
entries.abstract: Intermittency is a fundamental property of astrophysical turbulence because it concentrates strong gradients, dissipation, and transport into rare, localized structures. In the multiphase interstellar medium (ISM), turbulent driving is especially important because the balance between compressive and solenoidal motions can regulate how extreme fluctuations are distributed among thermal phases. Yet conventional increment statistics quantify intermittency without identifying the structures that host it. We analyze three matched ideal-MHD simulations of a thermally multiphase neutral medium that differ only in the compressive fraction of the driving. Density, velocity, and magnetic-field increments are non-Gaussian in every thermal phase. Increasing compressive driving redistributes density and magnetic fluctuations preferentially into the cold gas rather than uniformly enhancing them across phases. We identify the structures associated with extreme increments using local, scale-matched diagnostics of compression, thermal gradients, vorticity, strain, magnetic curl, and magnetic tension. Extreme magnetic increments preferentially occur where magnetic curl and magnetic tension are simultaneously enhanced, more strongly than extreme velocity increments are associated with their kinematic hosts. Extreme velocity increments show comparable enrichment in vorticity and strain, whereas extreme density increments preferentially trace converging flows and thermal gradients only in the unstable medium. These associations weaken beyond a phase-dependent coherence scale. Our results show that turbulent driving controls how intermittency is partitioned among thermal phases, while distinct physical structures host extreme density, velocity, and magnetic fluctuations.

entries.title: Untangling Similarities and Differences in Star Formation Histories Across Cosmological Simulations
entries.abstract: How galaxies assemble depends on processes ranging from small-scale baryonic physics to large-scale cosmological assembly, which are difficult to disentangle with observations alone. Using $\sim$63,000 simulated galaxies from seven cosmological simulations spanning hydrodynamical, semi-analytic, and semi-empirical models, we explore how specific star formation histories (sSFHs) vary across modelling assumptions. Using non-linear dimensionality reduction (UMAP), we find that sSFH shape variation organizes along a few smooth axes in a 2D embedding, broadly corresponding to (1) peak timing, (2) peak sharpness, and (3) subsequent quenching rate. We identify sSFH shapes that many simulations share ("common"), well described to first order by dark matter halo assembly, and a few tied to individual simulations ("unique"), which likely reflect subgrid and parametrization choices such as merger-triggered burst prescriptions. A notable exception is a common population of rapidly quenched galaxies found across most simulations, likely driven by e.g., active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback, that halo assembly alone cannot reproduce. The origin of the most distinctive unique shape, an Illustris-dominated history with an early peak and slow decline, remains unclear, but we test the effects of short-term variability. With a multi-objective auto-encoder neural network, we recover the simulation that a given sSFH is drawn from with $\sim$95\% out-of-sample accuracy; ablation tests indicate this information is embedded in long-timescale sSFH morphology rather than short-term variability. These results provide avenues for theoretical and observational follow-up connecting star formation histories to subgrid physical models.

entries.title: Intermittency in the Multiphase ISM --- II. Non-Gaussian Dust Polarization and Foreground Variance
entries.abstract: Interstellar turbulence produces non-Gaussian polarized Galactic dust emission whose higher-order statistics depend on thermal phase and turbulent forcing. We synthesize optically thin dust polarization from three thermally multiphase diffuse interstellar medium (ISM) simulations with compressive, mixed, and solenoidal forcing. We characterize the resulting non-Gaussian structure in the warm, unstable, and cold phases using $E$- and $B$-mode spectra, one-point distributions, scale-dependent increments, and Minkowski functionals. Both $E$ and $B$ modes are intermittent. Warm-phase emission remains closest to Gaussian, whereas cold gas shows flatter intermediate-scale spectra, broader non-Gaussian tails, and the strongest departures from Gaussian morphology. Compressive forcing generally produces the strongest projected intermittency, particularly in the cold phase and total emission, while mixed and solenoidal forcing show weaker signatures. These higher-order structures also enhance spatial fluctuations in polarized dust power: Gaussian fields matched to the same two-point covariance underestimate the region-to-region scatter by factors of up to $\sim2.6$. Our results show that thermal phase and turbulent forcing regulate not only the mean polarized dust spectrum but also the field-to-field distribution of foreground power, with implications for modeling Galactic foreground in CMB polarization measurements.

entries.title: Henrietta Leavitt's classical Cepheid relation
entries.abstract: The Leavitt & Pickering (1912) mean period-magnitude relation for SMC Cepheids exhibits correlated residuals relative to modern Gaia $B_G$ and Johnson $V$ photometry ($r_{δV/δL12}\approx0.76$). Therefore dispersion inherent to Leavitt's photographic photometry relation is not solely random scatter ($σ_{L12,B_G,V}=0.22\pm0.03,0.25\pm0.04,0.20\pm0^{m}.03$), and is potentially consistent with the partial encoding of combined effects from the elongated SMC, classical Cepheid instability strip, differential reddening, etc. OGLE data indicate that $\gtrsim870$ SMC variables identified by Leavitt (1908, Table 2) are classical Cepheids ($\gtrsim 90$ %), and the preliminary unphased Table 2 photometry likewise features correlated residuals relative to contemporary observations ($r_{δB_G/δL08-T2}\approx0.54$). Table 6 data in Leavitt (1908, $n=16$) define a highly linear Leavitt law over an extensive baseline ($r\approx-0.98$), but constitute a smaller sample than the later 1912 work ($n=25$).

entries.title: Internal Nucleon Properties and the Equation of State of Ultra-Dense Matter
entries.abstract: The question of the link between the nucleon properties and the equation of state of ultra-dense matter, both being composed of quarks and gluons, is investigated by adopting a soliton model to describe internal nucleon properties and a direct mapping between nucleon and quark matter to obtain the equation of state of ultra-dense matter. We compare $π+ω$ and $π+ω+ρ$ soliton models and analyze the presence of a pressure singularity at the nucleon center due to the $ρ$ field. This singularity impacts the equation of state in ultra-dense matter. Only the pressure derived from the canonical energy-momentum tensor has a singularity, while the Belinfante pseudo-gauge transformation of the energy-momentum tensor generates an internal pressure without a singularity. We then investigate predictions for the equation of state of ultra-dense matter based on different prescriptions for the nucleon pressure. It is shown that none of the prescriptions agree with the thermodynamical pressure defined in uniform matter. The mismatch between any equation of state and the thermodynamical one questions the simplicity of the direct mapping between finite-size nucleon properties and uniform matter as well as the role of the nucleon surface in the internal energy density and the pressure.

entries.title: What Does 2D Coronal Seismology Measure?
entries.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) coronal seismology based on coronagraphic imaging spectroscopy has emerged as a promising method for mapping the coronal magnetic field, but the physical meaning of its inferred quantities under optically thin line-of-sight (LOS) integration remains uncertain. We investigate this problem by synthesizing coronagraphic observables from a global wave-driven magnetohydrodynamic model with a long LOS extent and a structured corona, and by applying the same analysis procedures used for observations. We compare the diagnosed density, wave propagation direction, phase speed, and magnetic-field strength with different LOS-weighted reference quantities from the model. We find that the measured density and the wave propagation direction are both well represented by LOS emissivity-weighted quantities. In contrast, the phase speed is not controlled by emissivity weighting alone: the LOS distribution of wave velocity amplitude also plays an important role. As a result, the inferred magnetic field is better represented by combining the emissivity-weighted density with an amplitude-dependent effective speed. Emissivity weighting nevertheless remains a reasonable approximation, and a useful baseline, over much of the field of view, especially where the LOS does not cross strongly structured plasma-sheet-like regions. These results clarify the physical interpretation of 2D coronal seismology and provide guidance for future coronal magnetic-field tomography and model-constrained applications.

entries.title: Sulphur-bearing molecule survey towards prestellar and starless cores in the Perseus molecular cloud
entries.abstract: Sulphur is drastically depleted from the gas phase in dense starless and prestellar cores, creating the long-standing "missing sulphur problem". Observations of sulphur-bearing molecules are crucial to understanding sulphur chemistry, core-environment relationships, and the physical evolution of star-forming regions. We present a survey of four sulphur-bearing molecules, HCS+, OCS, H2CS, and SO, towards 15 starless and prestellar cores in the Perseus molecular cloud using the Yebes 40m telescope. The HCS+ 1-0, OCS 3-2 and 4-3, H2CS 1_{0,1}-0_{0,0}, and SO 3_2-2_2 transitions were observed, fitted with Gaussian profiles, and column densities were calculated assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE). We also compare these with observations of CS, CCS, and CCCS from a previous study. HCS+, OCS, H2CS, and SO are detected in 100%, 93%, 100%, and 73% of the sample, respectively. Derived column densities are (2.2-17.0)x10^11 cm^-2 for HCS+, (1.9-25.0)x10^12 cm^-2 for OCS, (1.0-15.0)x10^12 cm^-2 for H2CS, and (0.3-17.0)x10^13 cm^-2 for SO, spanning over an order of magnitude. HCS+ and SO abundances strongly correlate (inversely and directly, respectively) with core volume density, reinforcing their early- and late-type status. Correlations indicate a differentiation between carbon and oxygen chemistry for sulphur-bearing molecules, with CS showing the strongest correlations as expected. Cores in protostellar outflow paths do not show consistently higher abundances. The chemical age (SO/CS) correlates with physical age (volume density), except for Per752, an outlier likely linked to an enhanced cosmic ray ionization rate. These results provide a robust observational baseline constraining chemical models of sulphur chemistry in early star formation.

entries.title: A radio counterpart of the local little-red-dot J092359+415736
entries.abstract: Little red dots (LRDs) are compact red sources at z>~4. Broad lines suggest accreting black holes, yet radio and X-ray measurements are usually weak. Local LRDs allow multi-frequency, multi-epoch radio studies that are inaccessible at high redshift. We search archival radio images for a counterpart to the local LRD J092359+415736 at z~0.323, quantify its long-term radio variability, and identify the plausible origin of the radio emission. Flux densities at the optical position are measured in FIRST, LoTSS, RACS, VAST, and VLASS products spanning 0.144-3.0 GHz and 1994-2024. A compact 144 MHz counterpart is detected at 42sigma in LoTSS, coincident with the Gaia position, and is recovered in FIRST, RACS, VAST, and VLASS. LoTSS and ASKAP give a spectral index alpha ~ -0.30 +/- 0.11. The source varies on multiple timescales: FIRST at 1.4 GHz (1994) is a factor of ~2.6 below ASKAP (2021-2024) and below the extrapolated LoTSS-ASKAP spectrum, indicating long-term brightening over 26 yr; the 3 GHz flux density rises by 2.3sigma between VLASS epochs 2.2 and 3.2. A star-formation-only origin would require ~200 Msun/yr, against an unobscured H-alpha upper limit of 3.3 Msun/yr, implying an extreme obscured starburst. Ordinary radio supernovae and tidal disruption events are strongly disfavoured by the luminosity and 30-yr recovery, while refractive scintillation would itself require an ultracompact nuclear emitter. The persistent radio counterpart is best explained by accretion onto the central black hole. Among the three radio-detected local LRDs, this source is intermediate in luminosity and the only one with reported multi-year variability, adding a temporal dimension to the radio diversity of the class.

entries.title: Mergers may not be the main channel for galaxy stellar mass growth at redshift $z\gtrsim5$: Predictions from cosmological hierarchical models and simulations
entries.abstract: Mergers are a crucial channel of galaxy growth, but their role relative to star formation remains uncertain at high redshift. Here we investigate merger rates and merger-driven stellar mass assembly for galaxies with stellar mass $M_\star \gtrsim 10^8 \, {\rm M_{\odot}}$ at $z\simeq 5-11$, by combining complementary theoretical approaches within $Λ$CDM. These include the DECODE semi-empirical model, the TNG100 and EAGLE hydrodynamical simulations, and the \textsc{L-Galaxies} semi-analytical model, together with the Millennium and TNG100-Dark simulations used to examine dark matter subhalo statistics and merger timescales. This compares models with different treatments of baryonic physics and galaxy-halo connections. We find that dark matter-only simulations predict merger timescales $\sim 30\%$ longer than those inferred from cosmological simulations including baryons. Galaxy major merger ($M_{\rm \star,sat} / M_{\rm \star,cen} > 0.25$) rates are high at cosmic dawn and increase towards earlier epochs, reaching $\sim 1/{\rm Gyr}$ at $z\sim 5$ and peaking at $\sim 3/{\rm Gyr}$ at $z\sim 8$. Despite these high rates, mergers contribute only $\lesssim 10\%$ of the total cosmic stellar mass density evolution. The ex-situ stellar mass fraction ranges from a few percent to $\sim 20\%$ for all galaxies at $z\gtrsim 5$, across different models and simulations. Their broad agreement implies that stellar mass assembly at cosmic dawn is dominated by in-situ star formation rather than mergers. These findings suggest that the high pair fractions identified by JWST may not directly trace efficient ex-situ stellar mass growth, highlighting the need for physically motivated merger timescales to interpret galaxy assembly in the early Universe.

entries.title: Non-equilibrium chemistry and radiation hydrodynamics in metal-poor and metal-rich interstellar gas
entries.abstract: We present a flexible implementation of non-equilibrium chemical networks with the $\texttt{KROME}$ framework, coupled to a nonlocal variable Eddington tensor-closed radiation transport scheme ($\texttt{VETTAM}$). Our fiducial network is designed to explicitly capture the formation pathways of important molecular species such as CO, OH, and $\rm H_2O$, intermediaries like $\rm H_3^+$, and the destruction of these species through photon and cosmic-ray dissociation. We validate our scheme through benchmark tests, and demonstrate its success in 1D and 3D problems covering a broad range of metallicities ($0 \leq Z \lesssim \rm Z_{\odot}$) and densities ($n \lesssim 10^{17} \, \rm cm^{-3}$). We confirm earlier works that suggest that OH and $\rm H_2O$ are the key molecular species in dense gas ($n \gtrsim 10^{5} \, \rm cm^{-3}$) for $Z\lesssim 0.01 \rm Z_{\odot}$, dominate the cooling at these densities, and demonstrate that our scheme can reproduce their abundances with similar accuracy as dedicated static photo-dissociation region (PDR) codes. We also find that the dominant fine-structure coolant in dense ($n \gtrsim 10^3 \, \, \rm cm^{-3}$) PDRs transitions from CI to CII to OI at increasingly lower $Z$. Finally, we find that in turbulent media, rapid mixing at PDR interfaces renders the chemical species out of equilibrium, and show that this could potentially alleviate the long-standing problem of (static) PDR models producing excess CI in the diffuse ISM over UV absorption-line measurements. We conclude by presenting and comparing with alternative implementations of reduced but faster chemical networks in our scheme, discussing the problem-dependent performance-accuracy tradeoffs and future prospects.

entries.title: Observational evidence of black hole event horizon from ultra-compact X-ray binaries
entries.abstract: The event horizon is the most crucial feature that distinguishes black hole (BH) from all other objects in the universe. However, since no radiation can escape from the event horizon, its direct observational evidence remains lacking. Although both are compact objects, the event horizon leads to differences in the radiative behavior between black hole and neutron star (NS) X-ray binaries. Historically efforts to probe the existence of event horizons revealed that the BH X-ray binaries are fainter than NSs with similar orbital periods in their quiescent states. Here, we use a special class of X-ray binaries namely the ultra-compact X-ray binaries (UCXBs), to reveal the existence of the event horizon near stellar-mass black holes. In short-period UCXBs, gravitational radiation dominates the orbital angular momentum loss, allowing us to accurately determine their accretion rates. Based on five UCXBs with orbital periods shorter than 40 min, located in globular clusters, and identified accretors (NS or BH), we obtained their accretion rates. Combining their accretion rates and X-ray luminosities, we calculated the X-ray radiative efficiencies of NS and BH. The radiative efficiency of BH is about two to three orders of magnitude lower than that of NS systems, indicating the accretion energy is swallowed by the BH, thereby indirectly probe the presence of the event horizon.

entries.title: The Promise of Gravitational-Wave Astronomy
entries.abstract: We review the promise of upcoming gravitational-wave (GW) observations in addressing some of the important open questions in astrophysics and cosmology. A decade after the first direct detection of GWs, the field is entering a transformative phase driven by progressive detector upgrades and the anticipated advent of space-based and next-generation ground-based observatories. These instruments will not only push the distance horizon of GW observations to cosmological redshifts, but will dramatically extend the accessible frequency band, opening entirely new source classes that lie beyond the reach of current detectors. The source landscape is rich enough that surprises are likely. This review surveys our current understanding across this landscape and offers some perspective on the discoveries that upcoming GW observations are poised to deliver.

entries.title: Dynamically Coupled Three-dimensional Cloud-Chemistry in Rapidly Rotating Irradiated Atmospheres: an Application to the Compact White Dwarf-Brown Dwarf system ZTFJ0038+2030
entries.abstract: Clouds and disequilibrium chemistry shape the observable properties of substellar and planetary atmospheres, and JWST time-resolved spectroscopy now enables direct tests of their three-dimensional structures. We present an update to the 3D atmospheric framework ADAM, coupling the dynamical core to a miniature kinetic chemistry scheme (mini-chem) and a saturation-relaxation tracer cloud module. Using this framework, we investigate the atmosphere of the brown dwarf orbiting the white dwarf ZTFJ0038+2030 in a 10-hour orbit. The brown dwarf receives stellar irradiation comparable to its internal heat flux, placing the atmosphere in a regime where the circulation is characterized by a standing Matsuno--Gill wave response and equatorial superrotation. Rapid rotation confines these structures closer to the equator, producing more symmetric broadband light curves with smaller hotspot offsets than canonical hot Jupiters, in agreement with recent JWST observations of this system. Although most species are globally homogenized, rapid rotation limits global-scale horizontal mixing and allows circulation-driven vertical transport to maintain strong CO and CO$_2$ inhomogeneities in the photosphere. These chemical inhomogeneities produce asymmetric phase curves in the CO and CO$_2$ absorption bands, which could qualitatively explain the observed CO$_2$ light-curve asymmetry. When clouds are included, Na$_2$S clouds dominate the photosphere and weaken the large-scale circulation, lowering photospheric CO and CO$_2$ abundances, while MgSiO$_3$ and Fe clouds rain out at deeper levels. Because the dominant Na$_2$S clouds reside mostly above the quench region, cloud-driven convection has limited impact on the quenched abundances, which are instead regulated mainly by large-scale circulation.

entries.title: IC 1297: The Most Distant Known X-ray Planetary Nebula and One of the Most Luminous
entries.abstract: We present the first targeted Einstein Probe (EP) X-ray observations of any planetary nebula (PN). Using the onboard Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT), we detect X-ray emission within the central region of IC 1297. The spectral analysis yields a plasma temperature of $kT = 0.086^{+0.054}_{-0.058}$ keV ($T\sim1.0 \times 10^{6}$ K), characteristic of shocked wind bubbles in PNe, whereas there is no evidence that its Wolf-Rayet central star emits X-rays. The absorption-corrected X-ray luminosity in the 0.3--2.0 keV energy band is $L_{\mathrm{X}} = 2.8 \times 10^{32}$ erg s$^{-1}$, also consistent with a hot bubble. At an adopted distance of $\sim3.8$ kpc, IC 1297 is the most distant X-ray emitting PN found to date, opening up a new observational window on hot-bubble formation and evolution. It is also among the most luminous known X-ray-emitting PNe. Our results demonstrate the capability of the EP FXT for detecting and characterizing faint, extended X-ray sources in the soft X-ray band for distant PNe, extending the known spectral properties of detectable X-ray emitting PNe. We also compiled the X-ray properties of all 41 known Galactic XPNe, finding a clear correlation between distance and X-ray luminosity that reflects an observational bias toward detecting the brightest sources at large distances. The compilation also shows a separation in X-ray luminosity between hot bubbles powered by H-rich and [WR]-type central stars, with the latter reaching luminosities up to an order of magnitude higher. The ten most luminous XPNe all host [WR]/PG 1159 central stars.

entries.title: Phase Separation of HI in the Draco Nebula: CNM formation Triggered by Colliding WNM Flows
entries.abstract: We investigate the thermal phase structures and kinematics of atomic hydrogen (H I) gas in the Draco nebula to clarify how infalling H I evolves toward cold atomic and molecular clouds. Using the DHIGLS H I 21 cm data, we apply the Regularized Optimization for Hyper-Spectral Analysis (ROHSA) algorithm to decompose the emission into spatially coherent Gaussian components, and classify them as warm neutral medium (WNM), lukewarm neutral medium (LNM), and cold neutral medium (CNM). We identify two kinematically distinct WNM components: WNM1 near $-3$ km s$^{-1}$ and WNM2 near $-30$ km s$^{-1}$. The LNM forms a broad velocity bridge between two WNMs, whereas the CNM is concentrated within a narrower intermediate velocity range. CO emission is also confined to this interval and is associated with CNM-rich regions. The H I mass fractions are $\sim 41\%$, $\sim 23\%$, $\sim 17\%$, and $\sim 19\%$ for WNM1, WNM2, LNM, and CNM, respectively, with the LNM and CNM together accounting for $\sim 36\%$ of the total H I mass. No comparably independent WNM component is recovered at intermediate velocities, although a weak broad component may remain unresolved. The observed phase structures are consistent with a dynamically compressed multiphase interaction layer in which compression increases the gas density, shortens the radiative cooling time, and drives the evolution from WNM through thermally unstable gas toward the CNM. The present interaction may both create new CNM, and further compress or grow pre-existing dense structures. Our results provide the missing link between previous evidence for dynamical interaction and molecular cloud formation in Draco, and identify CNM formation as a key step in transforming gas accreting toward the Galactic disk into cold atomic and molecular clouds.

entries.title: Tracing the Influence of Distant companions on Exoplanetary Systems (TIDES) I. Highly Eccentric and Misaligned Binary Companions to Hot Jupiters
entries.abstract: The origin of hot Jupiters remains an open question. A significant fraction reside in binary or multiple star systems, suggesting that stellar companions may play an important role in shaping their present-day architectures. However, the orbits of the vast majority of these stellar companions remain poorly constrained, leaving their role in hot Jupiter evolution an open question. We present the Tracing the Influence of Distant companions on Exoplanetary Systems (TIDES) survey, a campaign to map the orbits of stellar companions in systems hosting hot Jupiters to assess the extent to which binaries play a role in hot Jupiter formation and migration. Here, we introduce our survey design and new orbital fits for the first six systems in our sample---$τ$ Boo, WASP-2, WASP-11, WASP-76, HAT-P-14, and HAT-P-16---by combining previous observations of the stellar companions together with new Keck/NIRC2 imaging and Keck/KPIC relative radial velocities. Among these six systems, the four with the most precisely constrained orbits exhibit high eccentricities ($e \geq 0.8$), and three of these systems also display significant planet--binary misalignments ($Δi \geq 20^\circ$). This suggests the orbital properties of stellar companions to hot Jupiter host stars are qualitatively different than field binaries and binaries hosting inner transiting small planets. These orbital architectures are consistent with stellar companions shaping the evolution of hot Jupiters, either through high-eccentricity migration or by participating in an earlier episode of dynamical evolution that ultimately led to hot Jupiter formation. Continued orbital monitoring of the full sample will reveal whether outer stellar companions play a causal role in the evolution of hot Jupiters.

entries.title: A breath of fresh air: Oxygen enhancement from silicate sublimation during early protostellar evolution
entries.abstract: Recently, an analog to the t = 0 moment of our Solar System's meteoritic record was identified for the first time around the Class I protostar HOPS-315. Crystalline silicates were found to recondense from SiO gas that cools as it advects upward from a hot thermostat region in the inner midplane. This t=0 moment may be associated with the formation of the first planetesimals in this disk. We explore whether HOPS-68, a Class I protostar with similar properties and system geometries, is engaged in such refractory recondensation as well. A detection of cooler gas-phase SiO in absorption above a hot disk midplane would allow us to achieve this goal, thanks to a previous detection of crystalline silicates. HOPS-68 was observed with the JWST MIRI and NIRSpec, showing multiple bands of molecular absorption. We use local thermal equilibrium slab models to measure the temperature, column density, velocity, and radial location of these bands. The molecular absorption bands of gaseous SiO, H2O, CO2, and 13CO trace a warm molecular inversion layer (300-500 K) at mid-altitudes above the hot disk midplane from 0.3-16 AU, which is consistently blue-shifted with respect to the system velocity by 33-53 km/s. Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of HOPS-68 kinematically resolve an SiO-rich jet and wind. We confirm that HOPS-68, like HOPS-315, is undergoing an epoch analogous to the t=0 moment in the Solar System's planet formation timeline. The detected warm molecular layer traces the base of a disk wind, which carries sublimated material from the thermostat region near 2 AU up into the outer disk. As for HOPS-315, the molecular layer in the inner few AU of HOPS-68 is enhanced in bulk oxygen as a result of this sublimation. Since HOPS-68 is less evolved than HOPS-315, this may indicate a prolonged epoch in protostellar evolution in which such oxygen enhancement occurs.

entries.title: Revisiting the Role of Global Magnetic Variables in Coronal Heating of Solar Active Regions
entries.abstract: Reconnection-based models of coronal heating predict that magnetic complexity---non-potential configurations, currents, shear---should enhance coronal emission independently of total magnetic flux. Previous work, however, found no evidence that complexity contributes independently to coronal heating (Fisher et al. 1998). We revisit this question using SDO/HMI vector magnetograms and SDO/AIA EUV imaging. HMI Space-weather Active Region Patches (SHARPs) provide 16 magnetic parameters characterizing field strength, gradients, currents, helicity, and non-potentiality. We measure spatially-integrated transition region and coronal emission using AIA 304A, 193A, 94A, and isolated Fe XVIII emission for 137 active regions, sampling plasma at ~0.09MK, ~1.4MK, and ~7.1MK. Partial correlation analysis isolates the contribution of each complexity parameter after controlling for total unsigned vertical magnetic flux. Unsigned flux (Phi_M) explains 72--82\% of variance in emission, following power laws (I ~ Phi_M^alpha, where alpha=0.61-1.19) consistent with prior soft X-ray results. Partial correlations reveal weak positive contributions (r = 0.2-0.3) to transition region (304A) emission from some vertical current and field parameters, but little evidence that other active-region-averaged measures of magnetic complexity enhance coronal emission. The exception is total photospheric magnetic free energy density (rho_tot), which shows a positive partial correlation (r = 0.49, p < 0.001) with Fe XVIII emission, but negative, or non-existent, partial correlations with other AIA filters. These results suggest quasi-steady coronal heating scales with magnetic flux, while rho_tot may contribute to high temperature coronal heating. At lower temperatures, regions with more stored energy than expected for their flux produce less EUV emission than expected.

entries.title: A0538-66: A transient ultraluminous X-ray source with a relativistic outflow, 69ms pulsations, and anomalous optical activity
entries.abstract: A0538-66 is a peculiar Be/X-ray binary in the Large Magellanic Cloud, hosting the fastest spinning neutron star of its class (~69ms) and showing the brightest optical bursts of any system of this type. We report four XMM-Newton observations obtained near periastron in 2025, together with MAXI and REM monitoring, and a reanalysis of archival RXTE data. On 30 September 2025 the source reached L_X~1.5E39 erg/s (0.2-10 keV), the highest level since 1980, and in February, May, and August 2026, MAXI detected similarly bright outbursts. During the XMM-Newton observation taken on 30 September 2025, we detected the pulsations, measuring P_spin=69.25878(2) ms and dP_spin/dt=6.58(9)E-10 s/s; the pulsed fraction was low (~3% in 1-10 keV), increased with energy, and the soft and hard pulse profiles were shifted by half a cycle. A new detection in RXTE data of 3 December 1998 gives a faster spin period of P_spin=68.88813(28) ms. The XMM-Newton/RGS spectra show emission lines from photoionised plasma at rest and blueshifted absorption lines that imply an outflow at ~0.12c. This indicates a highly super-Eddington accretion rate and an intrinsic L_X~1.5E39 erg/s, and it makes A0538-66 a transient ultra-luminous X-ray pulsar, a class of which only a few objects are known so far. Since 2023 the optical bursts observed by REM have become longer and brighter, resembling those of the 1980s, but most of them lack a luminous X-ray counterpart (L_X>1E37 erg/s). We interpret these results in terms of a radiation pressure dominated accretion disc whose geometrically thick inner regions intermittently screen the innermost emitting regions.

entries.title: Atomic hydrogen in $z=0$ galaxies in the COLIBRE simulations
entries.abstract: We present an overview of the properties of atomic hydrogen (HI) in galaxies at redshift $z=0$ in the COLIBRE cosmological galaxy formation simulations. COLIBRE directly simulates the multi-phase interstellar medium (ISM) and includes new methods to follow radiative cooling to $\approx 10\,\rm{K}$, non-equilibrium chemistry coupled to dust, and dust formation, growth \& destruction. We focus on the $(200\,\rm{cMpc})^3$ volume with resolution elements of $2\times 10^{6}\,\rm{M}_{\odot}$. No HI properties informed the calibration of model parameters and yet we find very good agreement with the observed $M_{\star}$-$M_{\rm{HI}}$ relation, the HI mass and velocity width functions, the HI mass-size relation, and (baryonic) Tully-Fisher relations, albeit with some mismatches at the extremes of the galaxy population. HI surface density profiles are realistic, except at large radii around massive ($M_{\star}\gtrsim 10^{10}\,\rm{M}_{\odot}$) galaxies where we find a population of possibly spurious circumgalactic HI clouds, whose abundances and masses decrease, however, with increasing mass resolution). Using smaller simulations to vary some of the uncertain model parameters, we find that the main scaling relations are at most mildly affected, although this may not extend to detailed HI morphokinematics. Convergence across mass resolution levels a factor of $8$ higher and lower is good: the median HI mass and HI `occupation fraction' as a function of halo mass, and the HI mass function, are remarkably stable, although the highest resolution model overproduces HI sources by a factor of $\approx2$ at $M_{\rm{HI}}\gtrsim 3\times 10^{9}\,\rm{M}_{\odot}$. Upturns in the low-mass and low-velocity slopes of the HI mass and velocity width functions with potentially subtle observational signatures are predicted.

entries.title: Simulating Ionospheric Distortions in Mock SKA-Low Solar Radio Observations
entries.abstract: The Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) will provide unprecedented angular resolution for low-frequency solar radio imaging, enabling access to fine-scale coronal structures. However, the improved spatial resolution of SKA-Low also increases the sensitivity of solar images to ionospheric propagation effects. We investigate the impact of ionospheric fluctuations on simulated SKA-Low solar observations at 50, 100, 150, and 200 MHz using the \textsc{Karabo} simulator and turbulent, moving ionospheric phase screens. We quantify the resulting image distortions using spatial power spectral density (PSD) analysis and compare the SKA response with corresponding MWA simulations. The results show that ionospheric distortions are strongly scale- and frequency-dependent, with the maximum fractional PSD distortion decreasing with observing frequencies. SKA resolves ionospheric fluctuations over spatial scales that are largely smoothed by the MWA instrumental response, with significant distortions occurring on scales comparable to solar active-region structures. These results demonstrate that ionospheric propagation effects should be considered when interpreting high-resolution SKA-low solar radio images, particularly at the lower end of the frequency band.

entries.title: Radio ghosts: Radio polarimetry study of newly discovered cluster minihalo candidates or radio tailed galaxies
entries.abstract: Extended diffuse radio emission in the central regions of galaxy clusters is commonly associated with non-thermal processes in the intracluster medium (ICM), but its origin and the mechanisms responsible for sustaining it remain uncertain. We present the discovery and multi-wavelength analysis of two diffuse radio sources, MKTJ0355-4237 and MKTJ0355-4230, to assess their nature and investigate their radio spectral and magnetic field properties through radio polarimetric analysis. We use deep MeerKAT L-band (1.28 GHz) observations to perform spectral analysis of the diffuse emission and study its polarisation properties via rotation measure synthesis. These are complemented by eROSITA X-ray data and DESI photometric redshift catalogues to characterise the host cluster environments. MKTJ0355-4237 is confirmed as cluster-scale minihalo with extent of $\sim 400$ kpc, while the other diffuse source MKTJ0355-4230 remain uncertain and could be either associated with a radio minihalo or radio tailed galaxy. Both show steep spectra ($α\approx -0.7$ to $-0.8$) that steepen toward the outskirts ($α\lesssim -2.5$), consistent with spatial variations in electron ageing and re-acceleration. Polarised emission is detected in both systems, with fractional polarisation $\sim1\,\%$ in the centres and increasing in the outer regions of MKTJ0355-4237. MKTJ0355-4230 is associated with a previously uncatalogued cluster and shows an X-ray morphology offset from the brightest cluster galaxy, indicative of dynamical activity. MKTJ0355-4237 exhibits a sharply bounded internal radio deficit without a corresponding X-ray counterpart, within current sensitivity limits. The spectral steepening supports turbulent re-acceleration as the origin of the diffuse emission.

entries.title: Finite-Temperature Equations of State for Neutron-Star Mergers within the Quark Mean-Field Model
entries.abstract: We extend the quark mean-field (QMF) model to finite temperature and systematically investigate the thermodynamic properties of uniform nuclear matter, using the relativistic mean-field (RMF) model as a reference. For each model, we consider two parameter sets calibrated to the same selected nuclear-matter saturation properties but with different nucleon Dirac effective-mass ratios at saturation. We examine the effective nucleon mass and the composition of $β$-equilibrium matter, together with the free energy, energy density, pressure, entropy, and heat capacities of symmetric nuclear matter, pure neutron matter, and $β$-equilibrium matter. The QMF and RMF models exhibit similar qualitative trends, but their predictions increasingly differ at high density, where the effective masses have distinct density dependences. These differences are particularly evident in the thermal pressure and thermal index. For the two parameter sets considered in this work, we further provide compact analytical representations of the thermal index, $Γ_{\rm th}(ρ_{\rm b},T,β)$ over baryon densities of 0.08-1.0 $\rm fm^{-3}$, temperatures of 5-100 MeV, and isospin asymmetries of 0-1. The fits reproduce the numerical results with an accuracy better than $2\%$ and can be directly implemented in binary neutron-star merger simulations. This study establishes a finite-temperature extension of the QMF framework and provides a basis for future assessments of how a quark-structure-based description of nuclear matter affects thermal support and post-merger dynamics in binary neutron-star mergers.

entries.title: Dynamical and thermal evolution of localized reconnecting current sheets under varying guide-fields in the solar corona
entries.abstract: Although magnetic reconnection in coronal current sheets (CSs) is a fundamental energy release mechanism in the solar corona, the role of guide-fields in governing its formation and self-consistent evolution is not fully understood. Through 2.5D resistive magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations, we investigate how guide-fields affect the formation and evolution of a localized reconnecting coronal CS. Strong guide-fields prevent oppositely directed field lines from approaching sufficiently to form a CS, delaying and suppressing its subsequent evolution. The reconnection rate exhibits a rising phase resembling a power-law, with exponent $δ_1$ decreasing with rising guide-fields, indicating slower temporal growth of the reconnection rate. The aspect ratio of the CS follows a similar power-law trend with the exponent $α_1$ decreasing with rising guide-fields. A subsequent slower growth phase of the reconnection rate shows a power-law exponent $δ_2$ that increases with rising guide-fields, as does the corresponding aspect-ratio exponent $α_2$. As the CS evolves, the latter phase is achieved due to a sharp decremental transition of the guide-field within the CS after a time when the increasing inflows are inefficiently resisted by the guide-field itself. In the reconnection regime during prior phases, the power-law exponents of the maximum temperature and the outflow velocities also decrease with rising guide-fields demonstrating that stronger guide-fields suppress the growth of these indicators also. This study suggests that a self-consistently formed CS displays phases of efficient and inefficient quenching of the reconnection mechanism, promoted by non-zero guide-fields. We also quantify this behavior for indicators of the reconnection process and discuss their applicability to observations of apparent CSs and probing background coronal conditions.

entries.title: MATISSE unveils a dusty disc in the interior of EP Aquarii. First evidence of a misaligned hierarchical triple system with a central AGB star?
entries.abstract: Aims. We have mapped the dust and molecular gas emission distributions in the vicinity (a few stellar radii) of the asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star EP\,Aquarii, with a previously reported stellar companion at $\sim$50\,au, to search for binary-induced asymmetries. Methods. We present an analysis of new high-angular-resolution ($\gtrsim$4\,mas) images obtained with MATISSE (in the wavelength range $\sim$3--8\,\mum) as well as archival high-angular-resolution ($\gtrsim$20\,mas) ALMA $\rm^{12}$CO\,(c$J$=2-1) line and continuum emission observations ($\sim$230\,GHz), to study the circumstellar morphology and kinematics of the molecular gas on these spatial scales. Results. The MATISSE images display a bright central source and two slightly extended emission features ("blobs") located on opposite sides of the AGB star (at radial distances of $\sim$4--10\,au). These structures are consistent with previous mid-infrared interferometric observations, suggesting stability over decades. The central source is elongated along the direction defined by the blobs, in both the MATISSE and ALMA continuum images. The ALMA $\rm^{12}$CO\,($J$=2-1) maps display an asymmetric inner wind with a velocity gradient. Conclusions. The observations are consistent with an edge-on dusty equatorial overdensity (disc-like), hinting the presence of a close ($\lesssim$4\,au) companion. The inferred symmetry axis is almost perpendicular to the CO velocity gradient and the orbital plane proposed for the distant ($\sim$50\,au) companion. EP\,Aqr may represent the first misaligned hierarchical triple system with a central AGB star.

entries.title: Low-frequency spectra and scattering of pulsars towards the Gum Nebula with the MWA
entries.abstract: Context. The Gum Nebula is a nearby ionised complex with sight-line-dependent pulsar propagation. Aims. We test whether a smooth ionised structure can explain low-frequency spectral turnovers and pulse broadening, or whether smaller-scale material is required. Methods. We analysed Murchison Widefield Array observations of six pulsars at 80--240 MHz, combining sub-band flux densities with literature data. We compared power-law, free--free absorption (FFA), and turnover-constrained broken-power-law (BPL) spectra, and modelled scattering through pulse-profile convolution. PSR J0820-4114 and the Vela pulsar were fitted jointly across frequency. Results. All six spectra depart from a single power law. FFA is favoured for PSRs J0737-3039A and J0820-4114, and BPL for J0742-2822 and J0835-4510; the other two classifications depend on assumed error floors. Conditional FFA solutions imply emission measures of $10^4$--$10^5$ pc cm$^{-6}$ for electron temperatures of $3\times10^3$--$10^4$ K, far exceeding smooth-shell expectations. PSRs J0737-3039A and J0837-4135 have scattering laws consistent with $τ_{\rm sc}\proptoν^{-4}$. We obtain $α_{\rm sc}=-3.07\pm0.11$ for J0742-2822 and $-1.59\pm0.44$ for J0820-4114 using a joint two-component model. The Vela pulsar is best described by an effective thick-screen model with $α_{\rm sc}\simeq-2.74$. Neither tested Galactic electron-density model reproduces both independent distances and low-frequency scattering uniformly. Conclusions. The results favour a structured Gum--Vela magneto-ionic environment in which neighbouring sight lines probe different absorbing and scattering material; these effects need not arise in the same plasma component.

entries.title: Fast Radio Bursts from Monster Shocks and Flares of Inspiraling Binary Neutron Stars: A Kinetic Model for Double Pulsar
entries.abstract: The coalescence of binary neutron star systems offers unprecedented possibilities for multimessenger observations, including the detection of gravitational waves, gamma-ray bursts, kilonovae, and potentially fast radio bursts. For a detailed investigation of the latter, one requires a kinetic plasma model to describe the interacting magnetospheres of the stars. We present a three-dimensional particle-in-cell kinetic simulation of the combined magnetosphere of a binary neutron star in which the two stars physically orbit one another so that the orbital motion itself twists the magnetic loops. We find that the stellar magnetic-field intensity ratio controls the emergence of flares, while the stellar spins set the direction and modulation of the flare. We identify four spatially and dynamically distinct regions of strong electromagnetic energy release: (i) an expanding fast magnetosonic wave that steepens into a monster shock, (ii) a plasma flare being pushed by (iii) an expanding fireball and containing (iv) a reconnecting current sheet. The fast magnetosonic wave is a promising source of coherent radio emission. It is released when orbital motion cuts a closed plasma loop. The electric and magnetic wave amplitudes are similar and reach that of the background magnetic field. Our kinetic treatment yields particle spectra and plasma structures that can be used to assess coherent emission in kinetic-scale simulations. In conclusion, the stellar orbital motion constitutes a driving channel distinct from models with spin-driven magnetospheric twisting.

entries.title: Massive black holes in the first billion years with JWST
entries.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope has unlocked uncharted territory for the study of early black holes, enabling the detection of fainter and smaller black holes at larger cosmological distances than previously possible. Compared to nearby massive black holes, they are characterised by several unexpected attributes, such as their multi-wavelength properties or their relation to their host galaxies. These observational findings challenge our understanding of the past evolution of present-day supermassive black holes, and provide novel anchor points to constrain theoretical models of black hole formation and growth. This review summarises our current understanding of the observed properties of newly discovered, active black holes in the early Universe, discusses the status of mass measurements and the relation to their hosts, as well as open questions and future prospects.

entries.title: Extrapolating Collisional Rate Coefficients for Molecules of Astrophysical Interest Using Neural Networks
entries.abstract: State-to-state rate coefficients for inelastic molecular collisions are essential inputs for non-local thermodynamic equilibrium radiative transfer models, yet their computation using quantum scattering methods is prohibitive for large molecules and highly excited rotational states. We investigate the ability of artificial neural networks to extend existing datasets of collisional excitation rate coefficients without performing additional scattering calculations. A multilayer perceptron model was trained using molecular quantum numbers, level energies, energy gaps, and kinetic temperature as descriptors, and optimized on logarithmic rate coefficients. The model was tested on diverse collision systems ranging from simple diatomic molecules (CO, SiO) to open-shell species (SO), small asymmetric tops (H$_2$O, SO$_2$), and complex organic molecules (benzonitrile and vinyl cyanide) colliding with H$_2$ molecules or He atoms. Extrapolations were performed toward higher rotational levels, higher temperatures, and combinations of both. For most systems, predictions of rate coefficients involving previously unseen rotational states yielded mean error factors between 1.1 and 1.5, with the dominant rate coefficients generally reproduced more accurately than weaker transitions. Temperature extrapolations proved particularly successful, while combined extrapolations in temperature and rotational levels remained accurate to within a factor of two in most cases. The prediction quality depends on the interplay between dataset size, temperature range, molecular complexity, and the presence of clear collisional propensity rules. Overall, the approach demonstrates that machine learning can provide a practical route to extending collisional datasets for astrophysical applications, especially for large molecules for which additional quantum-scattering calculations are computationally demanding.

entries.title: MUSE-DARK IV. Comparing Dark Matter Densities to Star Formation Histories in 375 intermediate-z galaxies
entries.abstract: (Abridged) Baryonic feedback is expected to transform cuspy dark-matter (DM) haloes into cores, but direct observational links between inner DM slopes and galaxy star-formation histories (SFHs) remain limited. We investigate and quantify the connection between halo inner slopes and baryonic assembly histories in a large sample of intermediate-z galaxies. We analyse 375 galaxies at 0.1<z<1.43 spanning 7<log(Mstar/Msun)<11.2 using 3D forward modelling of MUSE kinematics and disk-halo decompositions with mass-dependent (DC14-based) and generalised Navarro-Frenk-White (gNFW) halo profiles. Stellar population parameters are inferred from multi-band Spectral Energy Distribution fitting of UV-to-MIR photometry using a non-parametric SFH model. Bayesian model comparison shows that the DC14-based halo density profiles are statistically preferred over gNFW for a substantial fraction of the sample. The inferred inner slopes from gNFW fits nevertheless follow the DC14 expectation and reproduce the expected dependence on the stellar-to-halo mass ratio, despite this not being explicitly imposed. Partial correlation coefficient and random forest regression analyses consistently identify stellar mass (or, equivalently, the stellar-to-halo mass ratio) as the primary driver of the inner density slope, a result that holds robustly even when the analysis is restricted to the gNFW fits. In contrast, SFH-related quantities (e.g. formation time and 'burstiness' indicators) exhibit no independent predictive power on the DM halo inner slope once the dependence on stellar mass is accounted for. Cored systems preferentially occupy lower-mass, more bursty bins with later assembly times, whereas cuspy systems are associated with higher stellar masses, lower star formation activity, and earlier assembly epochs, in agreement with theoretical expectations of stellar-feedback-induced cores.

entries.title: EMU detection of mysterious multiple component radio-continuum emission from nearby spiral Seyfert I type galaxy 'Sand-timer' (NGC 7213)
entries.abstract: We present an Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) radio-continuum detection of the nearby spiral Seyfert I type galaxy NGC 7213 which we nickname `Sand-timer' due to its morphological appearance. We find intriguing, peculiar emission extending from the central supermassive black hole (SMBH), which we refer to as galaxy hyperbubbles and/or active galactic nucleus (AGN) jets. Finally, we find two previously undetected kiloparsec-scale features in the polarised intensity image, which appear most likely also related to the central SMBH, as restarted bipolar radio jets, though somewhat obscured in the radio-continuum total intensity image. They resemble the bow shocks often seen in Fanaroff-Riley Class II (FR-II) radio galaxies, and so we propose they most likely represent an early episode of the `Sand-timer's' AGN jet activity. An alternative scenario is that the core of NGC 7213 may be a supermassive binary black hole (SMBBH) undergoing a tidal disruption event (TDE), potentially causing the peculiar radio-continuum emission.

entries.title: Cell-based theoretical criteria on the onset and stability limit of thermonuclear detonation
entries.abstract: One of the key unresolved problems in thermonuclear explosions of white dwarfs (WDs), including type Ia supernovae, is the condition for ignition and propagation of thermonuclear flame. Given the limitation of hydrodynamic simulations in resolving the flame front involved in the explosion process, theoretical considerations for these criteria merit accurate prediction of the onset of deflagration and detonation (deflagration-to-detonation transition or direct initiation) and subsequent stable propagation. Application of cell-based theories, which are originally designed for terrestrial detonation incorporating the size of the cellular structure, to pure-helium detonation in a WD envelope was proven to be powerful. In the present work, we extend this for detonation in helium-carbon and carbon-oxygen mixtures, both of which are associated with the double-detonation model for type Ia supernovae. Comparing with previous hydrodynamic studies in terms of the minimum initiation energy and critical stellar mass for stable propagation, the agreement is satisfactory. For the helium-carbon detonation, it is theoretically substantiated that even an extremely low-mass WD envelope $\sim 10^{-3}$ M$_{\odot}$ can accommodate stable detonation. For the carbon-oxygen detonation, the oxygen-scale cell width is shown to be a good diagnosing indicator. In addition, it is indicated that direct initiation of the carbon-oxygen detonation is only available for a WD heavier than 0.6 M$_\odot$. The findings of this study enable first-order calibration of the explosion model by a simple calculation through the analogy between astrophysical and terrestrial burning, the latter of which can be tested and observed in a laboratory-scale experiment.

entries.title: Two sides of the same spin: tracking optical and radio pulsations of SAX J1808.4-3658 from outburst to quiescence
entries.abstract: High-time-resolution optical and UV observations have revealed bright coherent pulsations from accreting millisecond pulsars, exceeding the luminosity expected from thermal emission from NS hotspots or X-ray reflection by the accretion disk. Characterizing optical pulsations over a wide range of accretion rates through coordinated multi-wavelength observations can shed light on their origin. We present a timing study of the AMSP SAX J1808.4-3658 during its 2022 outburst and quiescence, using optical TNG/SiFAP2 observations, simultaneous NICER X-ray data, LCO optical monitoring, and MeerKAT radio observations in quiescence. During the outburst, we detect coherent optical pulsations with pulsed luminosities of 1.3x10^(30)erg/s. Combined with previous detections, our results suggest that the optical pulsed amplitude increases as the X-ray flux decreases. The X-ray and optical pulsed luminosities show opposite trends with X-ray luminosity, suggesting different responses to changes in the accretion rate.
